emb:L2034770363.clinical_problem: automatic segmentation of the newborn skeleton for maternal pelvis / fetal skeletal modeling
emb:L2034770363.model_description: The model takes 3D point clouds reconstructed from CT scans of newborn skeletons as input and outputs an automatic segmentation of skeletal parts. It was trained using PointNet++, a geometric deep learning architecture, on manually segmented CT scans from 124 newborns, and compared against a k-means clustering baseline. It is intended to speed up creation of articulated newborn skeleton models for maternal pelvis / fetal biomechanical modeling.
emb:L2034770363.headline_result: PointNet++ accuracy 95.7 ± 4.7% and IoU 91.7 ± 7.9%, vs 74.6 ± 3.7% accuracy and 59.8 ± 4.7% IoU for k-means clustering

emb:L2034817275.clinical_problem: imaging evaluation of pediatric musculoskeletal system diseases
emb:L2034817275.model_description: A narrative review of imaging techniques for pediatric musculoskeletal disease, covering CT (3D reconstruction, vascular imaging, dual-energy CT, iterative reconstruction for dose reduction) and MRI (non-radiation, multiparameter, high resolution for assessing bone development), and summarizing progress in computer-aided detection and diagnosis based on artificial intelligence combined with CT and MRI for these diseases.

emb:L2034817281.clinical_problem: AI-assisted diagnosis of pediatric bone and joint disease
emb:L2034817281.patient_population: children with osteoarticular (bone and joint) disease
emb:L2034817281.model_description: A narrative review summarizing progress of artificial intelligence in pediatric bone and joint imaging, covering image identification and analysis, lesion detection and classification, and intelligent auxiliary diagnostic systems, incorporating machine learning and radiomics combined with natural language processing.

emb:L2035162765.exclusion_reason: pediatric population not specified; study uses general/benchmark brain tumor MRI datasets (BRATS, Kaggle)

emb:L2035888469.model_family: Google Vision AutoML (transfer learning image classification)
emb:L2035888469.patient_population: 190 pediatric patients referred for liver biopsy and ultrasound
emb:L2035888469.model_description: B-mode ultrasound images of the liver (about 14 per patient) were used to train a supervised image-classification model on a cloud-based AI platform (Google Vision AutoML) via transfer learning, to classify liver appearance as fibrotic or non-fibrotic. The model's output was compared against biopsy-proven fibrosis status and against blinded pediatric radiologist reads on an external validation cohort.
emb:L2035888469.release_evidence: built using a commercial cloud platform (Google Vision AutoML), but the resulting model itself is not stated to be released
emb:L2035888469.dataset_size: 190 patients; 2,324 images (development, 154 cases) and 360 images (external validation, 36 cases)
emb:L2035888469.headline_result: External validation: AI sensitivity 70.56% vs radiologists' mean sensitivity 42.04%; AI accuracy 57.78% vs radiologists' mean accuracy 46.11%

emb:L2036026853.clinical_problem: prenatal detection and diagnosis of congenital heart disease
emb:L2036026853.model_description: A narrative review of 28 studies applying artificial intelligence to fetal cardiac ultrasound, covering automated generation and identification of standard fetal cardiac views and automated detection of congenital heart disease lesions, and discussing training-data and image-segmentation challenges.

emb:L2036650024.patient_population: children referred for left hand and wrist radiographs for bone age assessment at a tertiary centre in Hong Kong, Jan-Dec 2019, mean chronological age 9.8 years
emb:L2036650024.model_description: Left hand and wrist radiographs were analyzed by BoneXpert 3.0, an automated AI bone-age software using the Greulich and Pyle method, and compared against bone ages assessed manually by two experienced pediatric radiologists in 99 studies.
emb:L2036650024.headline_result: Strong correlation between BoneXpert and manual assessment (r = 0.98, R2 = 0.97); mean difference -0.08 year (SD 0.73); accuracy 0.74 year overall

emb:L2036663491.model_family: AI pneumonia CT image-assisted diagnostic analysis software
emb:L2036663491.clinical_problem: quantification of pneumonia lesion extent on chest CT in mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia
emb:L2036663491.patient_population: 85 children with mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia confirmed by nucleic acid test
emb:L2036663491.model_description: AI-assisted chest CT image analysis software automatically quantified lesion volume, percentage of lesion volume relative to total lung volume, and CT attenuation value on CT scans of children with confirmed mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia. These quantitative parameters were then correlated with clinical laboratory markers of inflammation.
emb:L2036663491.headline_result: Lesion volume and lesion volume percentage positively correlated with serum sialic acid, CRP, D-dimer, FDP and fibrinogen (r=0.232-0.439)

emb:L2036949000.clinical_problem: AI-assisted diagnosis of pediatric diseases on ultrasound
emb:L2036949000.model_description: A narrative review of the current status and progress of artificial intelligence applications in ultrasound-assisted diagnosis of pediatric diseases, noting that children have a disease spectrum distinct from adults.

The radiologist initially missed the nodules on first read, but the AI tool successfully identified them; the nodules were then confirmed and resected surgically.
emb:L2027698602.headline_result: AI-assisted diagnosis identified small lung nodules missed by the radiologist on initial chest CT read in both cases

emb:L2028194741.clinical_problem: brain age (biological age) prediction and longitudinal tracking as a biomarker of neurodevelopment
emb:L2028194741.patient_population: healthy children and adolescents through adulthood, ages 3-30, from 16 multisite datasets
emb:L2028194741.model_description: T1-weighted brain MRI scans (32,851 scans from 16 multisite datasets, ages 3-30) were used to train several deep-learning brain-age models, including a novel regression diffusion network (AgeDiffuse), to predict biological brain age from a structural MRI. The model was externally validated on separate multisite cohorts and used to track individual longitudinal brain-age changes over time; the code was made publicly available.
emb:L2028194741.release_evidence: "we made AgeDiffuse publicly available and usable for the research community"
emb:L2028194741.dataset_size: 32,851 T1-weighted MRI scans from 16 multisite datasets
emb:L2028194741.headline_result: Mean absolute error 2.78 years (IQR 1.2-3.9) in first external validation (5 datasets); 1.97 years (IQR 0.8-2.8) in second external validation (3 datasets)

emb:L2026972422.model_family: hybrid deep learning model with PCA-based feature selection and merging
emb:L2026972422.clinical_problem: detection of respiratory disorders in neonates
emb:L2026972422.patient_population: neonates hospitalized in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
emb:L2026972422.model_description: Chest X-ray images from neonates hospitalized in the NICU were used to train an enhanced hybrid deep learning model (C+EffxNet) to detect the presence of respiratory disorders, with PCA-selected features combined before binary classification. The same approach was also applied to a publicly available pediatric pneumonia chest X-ray dataset.
emb:L2026972422.dataset_size: neonatal NICU chest X-ray dataset and a public pediatric pneumonia chest X-ray dataset
emb:L2026972422.headline_result: Accuracy 0.977 and kappa 0.935 after feature merging on the neonatal dataset; accuracy 0.992 and kappa 0.982 on the pediatric pneumonia dataset

emb:L2028024972.clinical_problem: detection/prediction of pediatric obsessive-compulsive disorder using neuroimaging and biomarkers
emb:L2028024972.model_description: A narrative review analyzing machine learning approaches for detecting pediatric obsessive-compulsive disorder using neuroimaging biomarkers and oxidative stress biomarkers, describing challenges to prediction accuracy and research gaps in the literature.

emb:L2027952319.exclusion_reason: basic neuroscience classification research using fMRI connectivity in ADHD, not a diagnostic radiology application

emb:L2027951023.model_family: unsupervised deep-learning diffeomorphic registration convolutional neural network
emb:L2027951023.clinical_problem: correction of susceptibility artifacts in diffusion brain MRI
emb:L2027951023.patient_population: brain diffusion MRI scans spanning neonatal, child, adult and traveling participants
emb:L2027951023.model_description: SACNet is an unsupervised learning-based image registration network that corrects susceptibility artifacts (geometric and intensity distortion) in diffusion brain MRI acquired with single-shot echo planar imaging, across various phase-encoding protocols. It generates smooth diffeomorphic warps, optionally guided by neuroanatomy, and was evaluated on nearly 2,000 brain scans spanning neonates through adults, including multicenter data.
emb:L2027951023.release_evidence: "we also created easy-to-use command lines incorporating containerization techniques for quick user deployment" (no explicit statement of a public code repository)
emb:L2027951023.headline_result: State-of-the-art correction performance, effectively eliminating susceptibility-artifact-related multicenter effects compared with existing correction methods

emb:L2027950183.model_family: machine learning on functional connectome gradients (task-free fMRI)
emb:L2027950183.clinical_problem: prediction of neurodevelopmental (cognitive) outcome in infancy from neonatal brain imaging
emb:L2027950183.patient_population: 39 preterm and term babies, postmenstrual age 31-42 weeks
emb:L2027950183.model_description: Task-free functional MRI was used to compute sensorimotor-to-visual connectome gradients in preterm and term babies. Machine learning models were applied to these gradient measures at birth to predict individual cognitive outcomes at 2-year follow-up.
emb:L2027950183.headline_result: Connectome gradient at birth significantly predicted individual cognitive outcomes at 2-year follow-up

emb:L2024275090.clinical_problem: assessment of neonatal respiratory status and need for respiratory support using lung ultrasound
emb:L2024275090.patient_population: 62 newborns, gestational age >=33+0 weeks, with early tachypnea/dyspnea/oxygen requirement, multicentre
emb:L2024275090.model_description: Lung ultrasound scans obtained at defined early time points in newborns with respiratory distress were processed to extract regions of interest and used to train a neural network to interpret lung ultrasound and generate an AI-based score analogous to an established neonatal lung ultrasound score (nLUS). The AI score's ability to predict need for CPAP and surfactant therapy was compared with the established nLUS score.
emb:L2024275090.release_evidence: described as a research model with no stated public release
emb:L2024275090.dataset_size: 62 newborns, three lung ultrasound scans each
emb:L2024275090.headline_result: AUROC 0.88 (T0) and 0.80 (T1) for predicting need for CPAP; AUROC 0.84 (T0) and 0.89 (T1) for predicting need for surfactant therapy

emb:L2025163898.exclusion_reason: study population age not stated; pediatric onset of spondylolisthesis mentioned only as background

emb:L2025894160.model_family: Modified Faster Region Convolutional Neural Network with Cheetah Optimizer, using a GAN for segmentation
emb:L2025894160.model_description: Fetal spine ultrasound images obtained around the 18th week of pregnancy are preprocessed (contrast enhancement, denoising), segmented with a generative adversarial network to emphasize defective regions, and classified with a modified Faster R-CNN optimized by a Cheetah Optimizer algorithm to label images as normal or showing spina bifida.

emb:L2026173967.clinical_problem: recognition of standard imaging views in pediatric echocardiography
emb:L2026173967.model_description: EDMAE is a self-supervised model pretrained with a masked-autoencoder proxy task on a large private dataset of pediatric echocardiography images, then fine-tuned to recognize 27 standard echocardiographic views. It was also evaluated on a downstream cardiac ultrasound segmentation task using the public CAMUS dataset, and outperformed other supervised and self-supervised methods.
emb:L2026173967.headline_result: High classification accuracy across 27 standard pediatric echocardiography views; outperformed compared supervised and self-supervised methods on downstream CAMUS segmentation task

emb:L2026275343.model_family: AlexNet and VGG-19 feature fusion with multi-layer perceptron
emb:L2026275343.clinical_problem: automated identification of standard fetal ultrasound planes during obstetric examination
emb:L2026275343.model_description: Deep features extracted from AlexNet and VGG-19 (via global average pooling) are fused and fed into a multi-layer perceptron to automatically classify maternal-fetal ultrasound images into six standard plane categories, aiming to reduce the time and skill needed to acquire correct standard planes.
emb:L2026275343.headline_result: Achieved higher classification efficiency (accuracy, recall, precision, F1) than other existing state-of-the-art models on a common maternal-fetal ultrasound plane dataset

emb:L2027304409.model_family: modified U-Net segmentation with radiomics-based machine learning classifiers
emb:L2027304409.clinical_problem: noninvasive prediction of MYCN gene amplification status in neuroblastoma
emb:L2027304409.patient_population: 47 pediatric patients with neuroblastoma treated at a tertiary children's hospital, 2009-2020
emb:L2027304409.model_description: Pretreatment contrast-enhanced CT scans of children with neuroblastoma were automatically segmented with a modified U-Net, radiomic texture features were extracted and harmonized across scanners (ComBat), and machine-learning classifiers used the selected features to predict MYCN gene amplification status.
emb:L2027304409.headline_result: Median Dice score 0.728 (train) / 0.680 (test) for segmentation; top classifier achieved weighted F1 97%, AUC 96.9%, accuracy 96.97% for MYCN amplification classification

emb:L2027976250.model_family: improved DenseNet (lightweight), compared to DenseNet121, InceptionV3, MobileNetV3
emb:L2027976250.clinical_problem: automatic identification of standard views in pediatric echocardiography

emb:L2025488478.model_family: deep convolutional neural networks (Cold-start, Warm-start, Shrink-and-Perturb initialization) with weight-level ensembling
emb:L2025488478.clinical_problem: generalizability of chest X-ray classification models across adult and pediatric populations
emb:L2025488478.patient_population: adult and pediatric chest X-ray datasets, including external validation cohorts
emb:L2025488478.model_description: The study compares three deep-learning model initialization strategies (Cold-start, Warm-start, Shrink-and-Perturb) for chest X-ray classification models trained on periodically arriving data, evaluating generalizability on external adult and pediatric chest X-ray datasets, and proposes two weight-level ensembling methods to combine multiple trained models.
emb:L2025488478.headline_result: ImageNet-pretrained initialization showed superior generalizability over random initialization; weight-level ensembles showed significantly higher recall (p<0.05) than individual models

emb:L2025034717.model_description: A narrative review of the clinical application and prospects of artificial intelligence in prenatal ultrasound, discussing developments enabled by cloud computing and deep learning and the challenges and opportunities of clinical adoption.

emb:L2026025093.model_description: A narrative review of artificial intelligence and image-recognition technology applied to anteroposterior pelvic radiographs for the auxiliary diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip, summarizing technical challenges and future directions for intelligent, automatic diagnosis.

emb:L2024974897.model_family: off-the-shelf deep learning models and a custom shallow CNN, pretrained on adult MRI, with joint image-age fusion
emb:L2024974897.clinical_problem: classification of pediatric brain tumor type
emb:L2024974897.patient_population: 181 subjects from the Children's Brain Tumor Network (CBTN), infratentorial and supratentorial tumors, mainly low-grade astrocytoma, ependymoma, and medulloblastoma
emb:L2024974897.model_description: T1w-Gd, T2-weighted, and ADC MRI sequences from children with brain tumors were used, separately, to classify tumor type using four off-the-shelf deep learning models and a custom shallow network, all pretrained on adult MRI. Image and age data were combined with joint fusion, and tumor-type prediction was computed per tumor volume; model attention was assessed with Grad-CAM.
emb:L2024974897.headline_result: Best performance (custom shallow network with age fusion): MCC 0.71 (ADC) / 0.64 (T2-w) for infratentorial tumors; MCC 0.70 (ADC) / 0.57 (T2-w) for combined infra- and supratentorial tumors

emb:L2025454820.model_description: A narrative review of the research status and progress of deep-learning-based artificial intelligence for automatic bone age assessment in children and adolescents, noting that most current deep-learning bone-age research remains at the experimental stage.

emb:L2024913686.model_family: hybrid Greulich-Pyle and modified Tanner-Whitehouse deep learning model
emb:L2024913686.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in young children
emb:L2024913686.patient_population: 453 hand radiographs from a single institution (external validation), young children
emb:L2024913686.model_description: A hybrid Greulich-Pyle / modified Tanner-Whitehouse deep-learning model for bone age assessment was trained on an open dataset with an added carpal-bone analysis module (M1), and compared with a version without carpal-bone analysis (M2). Both were externally validated against a reference standard set by three human experts on 453 hand radiographs from a single institution, stratified by sex and pubertal developmental stage.
emb:L2024913686.headline_result: M1 (with carpal bone analysis) showed lower mean absolute difference (0.366y) than M2 (without, 0.388y) vs reference standard, p<0.001; greater improvement in pre-pubertal patients
